title: The call diagonal as an earnings trade: three bets in one
summary: A diagonal combines a vertical call spread and a calendar spread. It makes three bets: term structure (one-week vol rich versus one-month), implied volatility (a call diagonal is net long vega), and direction (the strike difference). If the stock drops after earnings, the speaker covers the short leg at 80-90% of its max profit and waits for a rebound.

steps.caption: Apple before earnings. Buy a one-month call, sell a one-week call at a higher strike.
The strike difference sets the directional bet.
Two legs with two expiries: a vertical spread and a calendar spread in one.
At the short call's expiry, the payoff peaks near the short strike.
The surface shows the long vega and term-structure bets: rich one-week vol is sold, cheaper one-month vol is bought.
If the stock drops, cover the short call at 80-90% of its max profit and keep the long call for a rebound.

takeaways: A diagonal is a vertical spread plus a calendar spread.
It bets on term structure, implied volatility and direction at once.
On a drop, the speaker buys back the short leg at 80-90% of max profit and waits for a rebound.
caveats: The speaker says this is educational, not a trade recommendation.
Earnings trades are event trades. The owner's X06 rule says do not pre-position for event moves.
Strikes, expiries and price are illustrative; the transcript does not give them.
Kept as a concept: the backtest engine has no event-timed diagonal structure.
